title: Making a doujin parody game as a first RPG , is it worth the effort?

posts.author: 46roneko
posts.body:
Hey guys!
First of all, I'd like to say that, although this is not my first project of making a game, it is my first RPG project. I've always loved RPGs, but I never developed one. It will probably be a short game, around 10 or 15 hours, nothing more than that.
That being said, I wanna start with a little background: I have developed games with original stories before, those who I wrote by myself, acting as story-writer and usually doing most of the game design (you can see these games in the website on my profile!).
Since I was young, I loved the world of Ragnarok Online. I've put countless hours into that game, both original servers (bRO, iRO, jRO, kRO) and also countless private servers. I've read the original Manhwa, as well as watched the terrible anime. I've played the DS game, and I've consumed several Ragnarok-themed doujin media, such as mangas, games, arrange albums, etc. I even played the weird spin-off titles such as Ragnarok Tactics for the PSP and Ragnarok Odyssey Ace on the PSVita. I love the graphical style (I've also played Gravity's other game made in ROs engine, Arcturus), I love the world building and it's story and lore. I love the character design and monster design as well! Lee Myung-Jin was really a genius.
However, I am aware that the popularity of this game has dropped and it is not as popular as it used to be, especially in Japan. Going to a doujin sokubaikai (doujin sale event, such as comiket) and trying to sell the game will probably not going to be a success because I bet most people have no idea what the game even is. I am not particularly worried about that, but I also wanted to sell the game in other places such as Steam or itch.io and that probably won't happen. I know selling parodies are definitely fine here in Japan, but that probably won't be the case for selling it on Steam or any other platform, so the game will probably stay "JDM-only" or either be completly freeware as a love letter to this game. The problem with it being freeware, however, is that I'm not on this alone. My girlfriend is helping me with the art part (in which I suck) and I wanted to sell the game so I could at least pay her a little bit of money.
Another reason as I wanted to make a parody game is that I have little to no experience in world building, and it might be easier for me to start writing an RPG story with a world that already exists and I am comfortable with.
But anyway... how do you, personally, feel about this? Some people say that making a fan-game or a parody game is a waste of time and effort, that you should focus on doing your own world building, but I really feel like I want to explore this world a lot with characters of my own and a story of my own.

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
I always suggest making your own game rather than a parody.
I'd much rather play a game that took heavy inspiration from something I liked, or, better yet, a new and original concept that's cool in different ways.
You'd also get to sell it without any worries about legal issues (at least copyright related ones).

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
I should point out that 10 to 15 hours for you, the dev to play is not a short game by any stretch of the imagination. For starters, the time it takes the dev to play their own game is often 1/2 to 1/3 the time a player takes, so 10 - 15 hours for you will be 30 - 45 hours for most players.
Then to add to that, it usually takes about 100 hours in the engine to make a good 1 hour of playtime for players. You can do faster than that when you get more experienced in the engine, but when starting out this often works out to a pretty accurate rule of thumb.
So to meet that goal of 30 - 45 ish hours for a player to play your game, you will need to plan around 3000 - 4500 hours, maybe even more to account for testing.
I'd suggest an even shorter game to learn the engine first myself. And by short I mean like one town and one dungeon. Maybe ts a go slay that Ogre in the dungeon game. Short, simple.

That's an interesting review, thank you!
Yeah, I have done other games in RPG Maker before, both XP, VX Ace, and MV. I may have lost a little bit of the touch, but I believe that once I hop in the engine again, things will start to look familiar fast.
I don't understand, however, why are people so concerned about the development time of the game. Well, the game will be ready when it's ready.
Also about playtime, if 10 to 15 hours to me, the dev, equals to 30 - 45 hours for most players, then I will have the 10 - 15 hours playtime as the focus for the player and maybe a 3.5 to 5 hours playtime for me (keeping the ratio of 1/3).
Of course I am aware that me, the dev, will play the game way faster than someone that never played it before. I have developed several games and other software before, this is a well known fact!

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
The thing with fan games is that they can be struck down by copyright holders. I'm not against the idea of making a fan game as a way to learn your workflow for RPG Maker, like you said, it could save you time in the creation of a setting and whatever, but yeah, it
can
just end up being destroyed by the original copyright holders, and that could be heartbreaking, especially with all the time and effort any RPG is going to take to make.
also, as has been stated by people earlier in the thread, maybe aim for an even shorter game. Especially when you're starting out and are likely to have messes that you'll tangle yourself up in, and the bigger the project, the more that messiness is going to affect you and slow you down even more.

posts.author: bgillisp

So yeah if you have made a game or two before then it will go faster, and adjusting your playtime to match will also work most likely.
Was just a legit concern as I took about well:
That was roughly my time in ACE to make 1 finished game + 2 proof of concepts that didn't get anywhere else. The finished game my save going into the final battle is about 20 hours. Hawkzombie when he streamed it was at 48 hours when he got to the same point.
So I was just worried that if you did 15 hours you might need about 3/4 of that.
Oh and the finished game took me 5 years 3 months to make in the end.
